resources.string: Off by default: stay on the Radio page, keeping your search and expanded group while audio plays. On: open Playing after selecting a station or source. You can always open Playing yourself.

Pinned stations
The bundled catalog includes national, provincial and selected international stations. Up to 12 channels can be pinned as shortcuts; CCTV-13 is first among nine initial pins. Hold and drag a pinned shortcut to reorder it on Radio or Playing; both share one saved order without interrupting audio. Shortcuts and list rows show station names without added sequence numbers or source counts. Source totals remain in the source selector and Playing source information. Holding a pinned shortcut with touch, left mouse or a confirm key shows its menu at the normal long-press timeout, before release. Release safely, then choose an option; keeping the pointer held and moving starts reordering instead. Remote Menu and Move pinned station remain available. Only shortcuts move. Pinned stations also stay in their normal groups with a configurable color. The current station uses General > Playback highlight color; pin indicators and remote focus remain separate.

Groups and the station list
Groups start collapsed. Tap a group or press remote OK to open it; opening another closes the first. Changing search closes groups. A long open group keeps its name at the list top; tap that sticky heading to collapse it. Chinese-area groups appear above the international divider, with United States and United Kingdom first internationally. Unclassified groups are separate. Expanded channels use two columns on wide screens, one on narrow screens or with larger fonts. Station menus provide pin/unpin, a fixed logo picker, address editing and source selection. Playing shows pinned shortcuts in the lyrics area. National names and recognized region/country headings follow the app language; supplied station names and custom groups are retained.

Radio visibility and settings
General contains Show Radio, below the Library, Queue and Playlists visibility switches. It only shows or hides the Radio navigation panel. Playback, Playing shortcuts, Music/Radio switching, media controls, Radio settings and ongoing downloads remain available while hidden. Radio settings contains subscriptions, import/export, reset, return to music, pin color, buffering, retries, source fallback, logos and live status. M3U groups take precedence, with recognized country aliases combined; otherwise names identify regions, with unknown names in Others.

Import, export and reset
Export M3U saves the complete current list for offline editing. Import always asks whether to keep and merge or replace all current stations. Merge skips identical sources and adds different URLs to matching stations. Replace all keeps only valid file entries, including after restart; unlisted built-ins stay removed until Reset built-ins, and subscriptions are disabled until explicitly enabled again. Pins remain for saved IDs, including disabled subscription caches. Keep exported IDs when renaming. Reset restores the whole bundled catalog while keeping additional user-created channels and subscriptions. Imports never edit the source file or delete music.

Subscription overview
Subscriptions cache each trusted TXT/M3U feed independently. Presets cover China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, United States, United Kingdom, worldwide stations and CCTV television audio. Add a preset or custom URL, then update, disable, edit or remove that list. Updates are sequential and manual by default. Subscription refresh optionally checks overdue lists monthly, weekly or daily, only after a minute of foreground use and never during startup or in the background. Matching names or stream URLs share a station; different URLs become sources. M3U export is a flattened station list; ZIP backup also preserves subscriptions, the refresh preference and selected bundled logos. Limits and publisher information are explained below.

Live playback and sources
Audio uses the Internet, not an FM tuner. Stop disconnects; Play rejoins live audio. Rewind/forward selects the previous/next source of the SAME station without wrapping; unavailable directions are disabled. Local music keeps its 10-second seek controls. Radio has no recording or timeline seeking. Automatic source fallback is optional and bounded.

Station logos and downloads
Choose one of 12 bundled station marks, or Automatic to use a downloaded logo or the selected default. Listening downloads the configured station logo when enabled, or use Download all pinned station logos explicitly in Radio settings. Selected bundled marks need no downloads. Remote images are limited to 512 KiB and resized to at most 128 pixels; disk copies remain until cleared. Browsing, import/export and subscription updates never fetch streams or logos. Startup is silent by default; enabling General > Play automatically on app launch may reconnect the last station and load its logo, even with the Radio panel hidden. Broadcaster marks imply no endorsement.

Playback continuity and availability
Renaming, changing a selected logo or editing station metadata preserves an unchanged playing source, connection and buffer, including while connecting. Stopped radio stays stopped. Manual edits, imports and resets pause radio only when they replace or remove its selected source; local music is unaffected. Subscription changes and export do not interrupt playback, even if the current station disappears from a feed. Select a station again to use its new addresses. After Music controls and requested startup playback are ready, the catalog warms once in the background without streams, logo downloads or subscription refreshes. This reduces later local loading, not connection or buffering time. Showing or hiding Radio does not change playback; use Stop or Music to leave a broadcast. Availability depends on the broadcaster and network. Some supplied URLs are old or unencrypted; TDM Macau links may be unreachable outside supported networks.

Save the complete radio list to local storage or USB for offline editing, not just the search results or pinned stations. The UTF-8 M3U contains names, stable IDs, groups, logo URLs and every playing source; no audio or images are downloaded. Keep a station’s ID when renaming it. Import the edited file to merge it or replace the entire list.

The complete export exceeds the import limit of 1 MiB or 5,000 source entries. No partial list was written. A local ZIP backup can preserve the full catalog.

Restore the names, groups, logos and addresses of ALL bundled stations, including regional and international channels? Edits to those stations will be reset. Additional user-created channels and pins are kept. Radio pauses if its selected source changes; local music and its queue are unchanged.
The complete bundled catalog was restored. Additional channels and pins were kept.

Save as UTF-8 TXT/M3U/M3U8, up to 1 MiB, 5,000 source entries and 32 sources per station. Export M3U writes the complete current list in this format, without downloading audio or logos.

TXT: name,URL per line; commas inside the URL are preserved. Stable IDs use three tab-separated columns: ID, name, URL. A line Province,#genre# sets the group for following TXT channels.

M3U:
#EXTM3U
#EXTINF:-1 tvg-id="radio:cnr:zgzs" group-title="National",Voice of China
https://ngcdn001.cnr.cn/live/zgzs/index.m3u8

Optional tvg-logo="https://…/logo.png" is downloaded only during playback. #EXTGRP groups are supported. Repeat the same ID/name for each different source URL. Export repeats its metadata for each source; edit all entries of that station consistently. The last entry supplies the name and supplied group/logo. Empty group-title or tvg-logo restores automatic grouping or the built-in logo. Backslash-escape quotes and backslashes inside quoted attributes.

Import always asks: Keep and merge retains current stations/addresses, skips identical sources, and adds different sources to matching names. Replace all stations keeps only valid file entries, removing unlisted stations and old sources, including built-ins. Cancel changes nothing. Reset built-ins restores the bundled catalog.

Keep exported IDs when renaming. Known existing IDs take precedence; otherwise known URLs/names or normalized names match stations, even when a new list supplies a different provider ID. Use direct HTTP/HTTPS audio or HLS URLs, not web pages, local paths, nested playlists or HLS manifests. Custom headers are ignored. Only import trusted lists; HTTP audio and logos are unencrypted. Old URLs may not work.
